newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debts track U.S. assets higher.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debts track U.S. assets higher.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices on Monday extended Friday's strong rally with gains spread across all the countries. Advancing U.S. bonds and stocks bolstered investor sentiments in lively trading.
"The market is happy to ride on the back of U.S. bonds," said a cheerful Brady trader. "The market is very liquid."
Portfolio manages are moving out of cash and emerging markets get their share of investment funds, he said.
"Investors look into the medium term of three to six months and see no disquieting signs," said Marcelo Fleury, a vice president of emerging markets at Garban Corp.
Intraday ranges of Bradies were kept very tight, as any profit-taking was quickly absorbed by new buying, he said.
Fleury said there was a last-minute rush to get on the bandwagon before the widely expected vote on Brazil's Brady buyback.
Some traders, however, were skeptical that the government would buy back at this juncture when prices had been bid up after months of speculation.
Brazil C rose a full point to 66-1/4. Pars also gained 3/4 to 57-1/4.
Argentina got a lift from the International Monetary Fund chief Michel Camdessus endorsement of the economic program presented by the new Economy Minister Roque Fernandez.
Camdessus also revealed a tentative agreement for another Extended Fund Facility for the period from September 1997 to 1999. Argentina FRBs and Pars each added 3/4 to 80-5/8 and 55-1/2.

Higher oil prices amid Mideast tension is benefiting some emerging markets. But the bump should not be overstated, because world supply and demand has not changed much, said Jim Nash, Latin America economist at Nomura Securities.
"Prices may stay high for a month and the market tends to discount that," he said.
In the case of Venezuela, the danger is that the government might be lulled by the fleeting strength of oil into relaxing its monetary policy, thereby setting back the reform, Nash said.
Mexico Bradies got the least out of the general euphoria. A sluggish Bolsa and mixed macro-economic numbers kept some investors from adding new positions on Mexico, traders said.
Mexico Pars climbed 3/8 to 67-1/8 and Discount gained 1/4 to 82-1/2.
